mainTopic: How far a נדר against 'meat' reaches: the agent-consulting test, the dispute between the תנא קמא and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and why birds but not fish are included
overview: The amud opens by finishing אביי's point that even רבי עקיבא agrees an agent must consult before buying a substitute, and רבא approves it. The גמרא then asks which תנא disagrees with רבי עקיבא and answers: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. A ברייתא shows the תנא קמא forbidding head, feet, organs and birds to someone who vowed off meat, while רבן שמעון בן גמליאל permits all of them. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל also calls eaters of innards 'not a person,' and the גמרא explains this refers to buying them. The גמרא then challenges the תנא קמא: if birds are forbidden because an agent would ask about them, fish should be forbidden too. אביי answers that the person had let blood, so he can't eat fish, while birds are still possible if boiled well. אביי also gives a second case, a person with sore eyes, and explains that שמואל's saying that fish heals the eyes applies only at the end of the illness.

steps.title: Even רבי עקיבא agrees the agent must ask first
steps.stepSummary: אביי ends his argument: everyone, even רבי עקיבא, agrees that an agent has to check with the sender before bringing a substitute.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't רבי עקיבא agree that the agent needs to consult the sender?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes אביי's point with a rhetorical question. Even רבי עקיבא agrees that an agent must ask before buying a substitute item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not really asking anything. It means 'Of course he agrees.' An agent who buys a different item without asking has not done what he was sent to do, even according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.confusionAlert: This line looks like a question, but it is really a statement. It means everyone agrees the agent must ask.

phrases.english: Doesn't Rabbi Akiva agree
that [the agent] needs to consult?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי לָא מוֹדֶה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא דִּצְרִיךְ אִימְּלוֹכֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes אביי's argument from the previous part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even according to רבי עקיבא, an agent must consult before substituting another item.

steps.title: רבא approves אביי's teaching
steps.stepSummary: The teaching was repeated before רבא, and he said אביי was correct.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaching was said before רבא. He said to them: נחמני said it well.
steps.whatsHappening: Someone repeated אביי's teaching to רבא, and רבא approved it. This closes the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's approval gives אביי's point extra weight. נחמני is a nickname for אביי, so 'נחמני said well' means אביי was right.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי says even רבי עקיבא agrees that an agent must consult before substituting, and רבא agrees with אביי.

phrases.english: This teaching was said before Rava.
He said to them: Nachmani said well.
phrases.notes: נחמני is another name for אביי.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אביי's view is accepted: the agent must consult, even according to רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: Which תנא argues with רבי עקיבא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא disagrees with רבי עקיבא's opinion in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who disagrees with רבי עקיבא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It wants to know which תנא holds the opposite of רבי עקיבא's view in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי עקיבא uses the agent test: if an agent would ask about an item as a substitute, that item counts as part of the vowed category. The גמרא wants to find a תנא who rejects that approach.

keyTerms.meaning: a sage of the מִשְׁנָה period

phrases.english: Who is the tanna
who disagrees with Rabbi Akiva?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תַּנָּא דִּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא who disagrees with רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: the first opinion in the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The answer is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. A ברייתא is quoted, starting with the תנא קמא, who forbids head, feet, organs and birds but permits fish and grasshoppers.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, as it is taught: One who vows off meat is forbidden all kinds of meat. He is also forbidden the head, the feet, the windpipe, the liver, the heart, and birds. But he is permitted fish and grasshoppers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names רבן שמעון בן גמליאל as the one who disagrees, then brings a ברייתא to show it. First it quotes the תנא קמא's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא takes 'meat' broadly. It includes less popular parts like head, feet and organs, and even birds. Only fish and grasshoppers are left out.

phrases.english: It is Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
as it is taught: One who vows off meat
is forbidden in all kinds of meat,
and is forbidden in the head and the feet,
and the windpipe, the liver, and the heart,
and in birds,
and is permitted in the flesh of fish and grasshoppers.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הִיא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3 and begins the supporting ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is the one who disagrees with רבי עקיבא, as shown in the ברייתא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about one who vows off meat.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל permits organs and birds
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל permits the head, feet, organs and birds, and of course fish. He also says innards are not meat, and someone who eats them is 'not a person.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: One who vows off meat is forbidden all kinds of meat. But he is permitted the head, feet, windpipe, liver, heart and birds, and needless to say fish and grasshoppers. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל also used to say: innards are not meat, and one who eats them is not a person.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's opinion, which is much narrower than the תנא קמא's. He also adds a sharp saying about innards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, 'meat' means only regular meat, so the organs and birds are not included. This is why he disagrees with רבי עקיבא. For him, the vow does not include an item just because an agent might ask about it as a substitute.

keyTerms.meaning: a person, a normal human being

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
One who vows off meat
is forbidden in all kinds of meat,
but is permitted in the head and the feet,
and the windpipe, the liver, the heart, and birds,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר בְּשַׂר דָּגִים וַחֲגָבִים
phrases.english: and needless to say the flesh of fish and grasshoppers.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר
phrases.english: And so Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel used to say:
Innards are not meat,
and one who eats them is not a person.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר הַנּוֹדֵר מִן הַבָּשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who vows off meat may still eat head, feet, organs, birds, fish and grasshoppers.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the real disagreement. One side counts borderline items as 'meat,' and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל limits 'meat' to its plain sense.

steps.title: Explaining 'one who eats them is not a person'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא clarifies that for eating, innards are treated like meat. Only someone who goes out and buys them is 'not a person.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Those who eat them treat them like meat. As for buying them, the buyer is not a normal person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's harsh saying. It separates eating innards from buying them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling an eater 'not a person' sounds too extreme, so the גמרא narrows it. People who eat innards do treat them like meat. The criticism is only for someone who spends money to buy them.

phrases.english: Those who eat them [treat them] like meat;
regarding buying,
[the buyer] is not a person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the last line of step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Innards are treated like meat when eaten. The 'not a person' comment is about buying them.

steps.title: Why does the תנא קמא forbid bird meat?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the תנא קמא forbids birds: an agent sent for meat would ask about bringing bird meat instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is bird meat different, so that the תנא קמא forbids it? Because an agent does consult about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the reason behind the תנא קמא's ruling on birds. It is setting up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא uses the agent test, like רבי עקיבא. Bird meat is close enough to meat that an agent would ask whether to bring it, so it counts as 'meat.'

phrases.english: What is different about bird meat
for the first tanna, that he forbids it?
Because an agent tends
to consult about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא בְּשַׂר עוֹף לְתַנָּא קַמָּא דַּאֲסִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the תנא קמא's ruling in step 4 to examine its reasoning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the תנא קמא includes bird meat in a vow against meat.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An agent sent for meat would consult about bringing bird meat.

steps.title: Then fish should be forbidden too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reasoning: an agent would also ask about fish if he found no meat, so fish should be forbidden too.
steps.simpleTranslation: With fish too, an agent consults. If he does not find meat, he asks: 'If I don't find meat, should I bring fish?' So fish should be forbidden as well!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reason given for birds. The same reasoning seems to apply to fish, yet the תנא קמא permits fish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the test is 'would the agent ask about it,' fish should pass the test just like birds. That makes the תנא קמא's line between birds and fish seem inconsistent, and the גמרא demands an explanation.

phrases.english: With fish too, the agent tends to,
for if he does not find meat,
he consults about it,
saying: If I do not find meat,
should I bring fish?
So let them be forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reason from step 7 to challenge the תנא קמא's permission of fish.
steps.kashyaTarget: The תנא קמא's ruling that fish is permitted while birds are forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If birds are forbidden because an agent would ask about them, fish should be forbidden too, since an agent would also ask about fish.

steps.title: אביי: The person had let blood
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the vow was made by someone who had just let blood. Such a person doesn't eat fish, so fish would not come to mind as a replacement for meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: For example, where he let blood, for such a person does not eat fish.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question from Step 8 about why fish is permitted. He says the case is one where the person had let blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was that an agent would ask about fish as a replacement for meat, just like birds. אביי says that after הקזת דם people don't eat fish. So fish isn't a real replacement for meat for this person, and his vow doesn't include it.

keyTerms.meaning: for example; the case is one where

phrases.english: Abaye said:
For example, where he let blood,
for such a person does not eat fish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 8 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Fish should be forbidden, because an agent would ask about it just like birds.
steps.terutzMaskana: In this case the person can't eat fish anyway, so fish isn't a replacement for meat for him.

steps.title: Someone who let blood can't eat birds either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if the person let blood, he would not eat birds either. שמואל says that eating bird meat after bloodletting makes the heart flutter like a bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, he would not eat birds either. For שמואל said: one who lets blood and eats bird meat, his heart flies like a bird!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's answer. Birds are also bad after bloodletting, so the case should not explain why birds are forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא forbids birds because they are a replacement for meat. If this person can't eat birds either, birds should drop out just like fish. Then the תנא קמא's rule forbidding birds makes no sense in אביי's case.

phrases.english: If so,
he would not eat even birds either.
For Shmuel said:
One who lets blood and eats bird meat,
his heart flies like a bird!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ עוֹפוֹת נָמֵי לָא אָכֵיל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Birds are just as bad as fish after bloodletting, so birds should not be included in the vow either.

steps.title: Two ברייתות: birds are bad around bloodletting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up its objection with two ברייתות. Both list birds among the foods that should not be eaten around bloodletting.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught: one does not let blood on fish, nor on birds, nor on salted meat. And it was taught: if one let blood, he should not eat milk, nor cheese, nor eggs, nor cress, nor birds, nor salted meat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds two ברייתות to make its objection stronger. Both show that birds are bad for someone who let blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא says not to let blood when one is going to eat fish, birds or salted meat afterward. The second says not to eat a list of foods after letting blood, and birds are on that list too. Together with שמואל, this shows that birds are just as off-limits as fish.

phrases.english: And it was taught:
One does not let blood [and then eat] fish,
phrases.notes: "On fish" means right after eating fish.

phrases.english: nor on birds,
nor on salted meat.
And it was taught:
If one let blood,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יֹאכַל לֹא חָלָב, וְלֹא גְּבִינָה,
phrases.english: he should not eat milk, nor cheese,
nor eggs, nor cress,
nor birds, nor salted meat!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא: אֵין מַקִּיזִין לֹא עַל דָּגִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds sources that support the objection in Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That birds are harmful for someone who let blood
steps.raayaSupportSource: Two ברייתות listing birds among forbidden foods around bloodletting

steps.title: Birds can be eaten if boiled well
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that birds are different. Someone who let blood can eat them by boiling them well, so they are still a real replacement for meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Birds are different, for it is possible to eat them through boiling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends אביי's answer. Birds can be made safe by boiling them, but fish can't.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fish are completely off-limits after bloodletting. Birds can still be eaten if they are boiled well. So birds stay a real option instead of meat and are forbidden by the vow, while fish are not.

phrases.english: Birds are different,
for it is possible to eat them through boiling.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי עוֹפוֹת, דְּאֶפְשָׁר עַל יְדֵי שְׁלִיקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of Steps 10 and 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Birds are just as off-limits as fish after bloodletting.
steps.terutzMaskana: Birds can be eaten if boiled well, so they still count as a replacement for meat.
steps.whatToRemember: In אביי's first case (bloodletting), fish is off-limits completely, but birds are still possible through boiling. That is why the vow includes birds and not fish.

steps.title: אביי: The person had sore eyes
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives another case: the person's eyes were hurting. Fish is bad for the eyes, so fish is not a replacement for meat for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: For example, where his eyes hurt him, for fish are harmful for the eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a second way to explain why the תנא קמא permits fish. Here the vow was made by someone with sore eyes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer works the same way as the bloodletting case. Something about the person's health makes fish unfit for him. Birds don't harm the eyes, so they stay a replacement for meat and are included in the vow.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
For example, where his eyes hurt him,
for fish are harmful for the eyes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: כְּגוֹן דְּכָיְיבִין לֵיהּ עֵינֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the קשיא of Step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Fish should be forbidden like birds.
steps.terutzMaskana: A person with sore eyes avoids fish, so fish is not a replacement for meat for him.

steps.title: But שמואל says fish heals the eyes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that a person with sore eyes would actually eat fish. שמואל says fish is a medicine for the eyes.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, he would eat fish, for שמואל said: נוּן סָמֶךְ עַיִן: fish is a medicine for the eyes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's second case. It quotes שמואל, who says fish is good for the eyes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said fish is bad for sore eyes. שמואל says the opposite, that fish heals the eyes. If so, a person with sore eyes would want fish, and fish should be included in his vow.

keyTerms.meaning: the letters נ־ס־ע, a memory hook for the saying

phrases.english: If so, he would eat fish,
for Shmuel said:
Nun, samech, ayin:
phrases.notes: Each of these three letters starts one word of the saying that comes next.

phrases.english: fish is a medicine for the eyes!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי אָכֵיל דָּגִים, דְּהָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's second case in Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that fish is harmful for the eyes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל says fish heals the eyes, so a person with sore eyes would eat fish.

steps.title: שמואל means the last stage of the illness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמואל's statement is about the end of the eye illness. At the start, fish is harmful, as אביי said.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is at the end of the illness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the clash between אביי and שמואל. Each one is talking about a different stage of the eye illness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fish heals the eyes only at the end of the infection. While the eyes are still hurting, fish is harmful. אביי's case is a person whose eyes hurt now, so for him fish is off-limits and is not included in the vow.

phrases.english: That is at the end of the illness.
phrases.notes: אוּכְלָא here means the eye infection. שמואל's healing fish is for its last stage.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Fish is always good for the eyes, so the person would eat fish.
steps.terutzMaskana: Fish helps only at the end of the illness. While the eyes hurt, fish is harmful.
steps.whatToRemember: Both of אביי's answers work the same way: the person has a health reason to avoid fish but can still eat birds. So his vow forbids birds but not fish.
